blurb: GANs, diffusion, latent spaces, guidance, video models — and how to tell what's real.

cards.title: How diffusion works

steps.p: Take real images and add a little random noise, step after step, until only static remains.
Train a network to look at a noisy image and predict the noise that was added.
Start with random noise and repeatedly subtract the predicted noise. An image gradually appears.

cards.aside: Sculpting by subtraction: the model learns what to remove until only a plausible image is left.

cards.q: During training, a diffusion model's network typically learns to predict…
options: The noise that was added to a noisy image
cards.why: The noise. Knowing the noise means knowing how to remove it. Variants predict the clean image or a mix, but they are mathematically related.

cards.statement: Diffusion models traditionally produce an image in a single network pass.
cards.why: False. Classic diffusion takes dozens to hundreds of denoising steps. Distillation methods have since cut that to just a few for fast generation.

cards.q: Before diffusion, GANs led image generation. A GAN trains…
options: A generator against a discriminator that tries to spot its fakes
cards.why: An adversarial game. The generator improves by fooling the discriminator, which improves by catching it.

cards.title: Ian Goodfellow reportedly came up with GANs in 2014 after a debate with friends at a Montreal bar.
cards.detail: He went home and coded it that night, and it worked on the first try, according to his own account.

cards.statement: GANs are known for unstable training and "mode collapse", where the generator produces only a few kinds of output.
cards.why: True. Balancing two competing networks is delicate. Diffusion's simple, stable training objective is a major reason it took over.

cards.title: Stable Diffusion's design

steps.p: An autoencoder squeezes a 512×512 image into a 64×64 latent grid, about 48 times fewer numbers.
Denoising happens on that small grid, making generation far cheaper.
A text encoder turns the prompt into vectors that the denoiser attends to through cross-attention at each step.

cards.aside: This efficiency let Stable Diffusion run on consumer GPUs when released in 2022.

cards.q: Why does latent diffusion work in a compressed space instead of directly on pixels?
options: It is far cheaper, while the decoder restores fine detail
cards.why: Cost. Most pixel-level detail is perceptually redundant. Diffusing in a compact latent space cuts compute dramatically.

cards.q: Raising the classifier-free guidance scale usually makes images…
options: Follow the prompt more closely but with less variety
cards.why: Prompt adherence vs diversity. Guidance pushes predictions away from the unconditioned ones. Too high and images look oversaturated.

cards.statement: Stable Diffusion's weights were released publicly for anyone to download.
cards.why: True. In August 2022 Stability AI released the weights, sparking a huge ecosystem of fine-tunes, tools and controversy.

cards.title: Stable Diffusion was trained using LAION-5B, a dataset of 5.85 billion image-text pairs scraped from the web.
cards.detail: Its scale enabled broad visual knowledge, but it also included copyrighted and problematic images, fueling lawsuits and later dataset cleanups.

options: Steering away from the negative prompt's prediction during guidance
cards.why: Repurposed guidance. Guidance normally steers away from the unconditioned prediction. Using the negative prompt's prediction instead steers away from that content.

cards.title: From images to video

steps.p: Diffusion Transformers (DiT) swapped the convolutional U-Net for a transformer, which scales more predictably.
Video is cut into patches across space and time and treated as one long sequence.
Objects must keep their shape, identity and physics from frame to frame.

cards.aside: OpenAI's Sora, announced in February 2024, used a diffusion transformer over spacetime patches.

cards.q: Diffusion Transformers (DiT) replaced which component of earlier diffusion models?
cards.why: The U-Net. A transformer denoiser lets image and video models follow the same scaling recipe as language models.

cards.statement: Keeping objects consistent across frames is a main reason video generation is harder than images.
cards.why: True. A person's face, clothes and the scene's physics must stay coherent for hundreds of frames. Errors show up as morphing and flicker.

cards.q: Flow matching, used in newer models like Stable Diffusion 3 and Flux, learns…
options: Straighter paths from noise to data, allowing fewer generation steps
cards.why: Straight-line paths. Simpler trajectories from noise to image are easier to follow in few steps.

cards.title: OpenAI's Sora preview in February 2024 showed videos up to a minute long from text prompts.
cards.detail: Earlier text-to-video models produced a few seconds of often unstable footage. Sora's length and coherence reset expectations across the field.

cards.statement: Images can also be generated token by token, the way language models generate text.
cards.why: True. The original DALL·E (2021) generated images as sequences of discrete image tokens. Autoregressive and diffusion approaches continue to compete and combine.

cards.title: Proving where media came from

steps.p: Invisible signals embedded in generated content, like Google's SynthID, can be detected later by the right tool.
The C2PA standard attaches cryptographically signed records of how a file was made and edited.
Classifiers try to spot AI content from artifacts, but they are unreliable and easily fooled.

cards.aside: The most promising approach proves what is authentic, rather than trying to catch every fake.

options: Signed metadata recording how a piece of media was created and edited
cards.why: Provenance records. Cameras, editing apps and generators can sign a file's history, so viewers can check its origin.

cards.statement: Today's AI-image detectors are reliable enough to prove an image is fake.
cards.why: False. They produce false positives and negatives, and simple edits like resizing or recompression can defeat them. Treat their output as a hint, not proof.

cards.q: Why is provenance metadata alone a weak defense?
options: Screenshots and re-uploads often strip it
cards.why: Easy to lose. Metadata travels with the file, not the pixels. That is why it is paired with watermarks embedded in the content itself.

cards.title: Google's SynthID hides an imperceptible watermark in the pixels of AI-generated images — and in text too.
cards.detail: For text, it subtly biases word choices in a statistically detectable way. Google open-sourced the text version in 2024.

cards.title: Verify before you share
cards.body: A reverse image search finds where a picture first appeared and whether fact-checkers have covered it. It takes less time than resharing.
cards.challenge: Next time a striking image surprises you, run a reverse image search before reacting to it.
